title: Mapping the neuronal building blocks of human language with language models
goal: Surpass the source-paper result on the same task: Preserve the complete original model-to-neuron predictivity panel across all source participants, sessions and eligible neurons. Figure 3b population correlation supplies a reported numeric anchor; its relationship to the individual-neuron temporal/layer panel and controls must be fixed without silently dropping those intended outputs.
primary_outputs: Candidate method and outputs for the source task: Preserve the complete original model-to-neuron predictivity panel across all source participants, sessions and eligible neurons. Figure 3b population correlation supplies a reported numeric anchor; its relationship to the individual-neuron temporal/layer panel and controls must be fixed without silently dropping those intended outputs.

Source-paper comparison for Original model-to-neuron predictivity panel; exact primary reduction unresolved, with Figure 3b population Pearson r as a source anchor: Population predictivity is Pearson correlation between observed session population firing rate and model predictions under source sentence-held-out ridge regression. The paper reports mean 0.05 ± 0.01 SEM; artifact MAE and neuronal selectivity p-values are separate quantities.
success_criteria: Authenticate the exact original Figure 3b endpoint, full cohort and unrounded contextual author baseline before enabling paper-win admission.
Preserve all intended source sessions, neurons, temporal/layer outputs and controls; do not promote a convenient population-only subset to a win for the complete model-to-neuron task.
Retain the original sentence-held-out split, source embeddings, input exposure, response processing and layer/time/session reduction for candidate and comparator.
Require a justified positive improvement beyond baseline rounding and a predeclared participant-aware uncertainty rule; preserve lexical/shuffle diagnostics.
Native array reproduction, greater linguistic selectivity, a new model on the purged split or a newly equal-person-weighted score cannot count as surpassing the published 0.05.
The bound improvement contract must be improvement_ready and its complete same-task comparison and admission requirements must pass.
Reproduction is calibration only; reconstructing a numerical result, changing the task or split, or achieving stronger significance alone is not success.

episode.improvement_loop: Design only. After baseline/code mapping and access budgets are qualified, expose declared training/validation feedback for iteration on the original embedding-to-neural prediction problem.
episode.candidate_freeze: Freeze candidate code, allowed embedding families, original sentence IDs, preprocessing, layer/lag selection policy, Figure 3b reduction, resource caps and uncertainty before final evaluation.
episode.final_evaluation: Use an independent scoring implementation on the exact original support and published aggregation, preserving participant/session pairs and both rounded published and unrounded rerun scores. New purged folds remain an extension.
episode.baseline_policy: Keep the reported 0.05, the future authenticated original-author rerun, native artifact MAE and prospective operator baseline scores in separate fields; only a matched original comparison can support paper victory.
